ideas.hypothesis: City-level GDP growth rates, once rescaled by a few basic urban quantities (population density and trip connectivity of the street network), collapse onto a single universal curve, so a parameter-free scaling model predicts relative urban growth better than standard convergence regressions.

sources.role: method: rescaling that collapses city curves onto one universal curve with a parameter-free model
measure: S-shaped relative growth model for comparing economic systems
setting: growth of nodal centres and hinterlands within a metropolitan region

ideas.test: Panel of 200-300 metropolitan areas (e.g., OECD metro or Chinese prefecture-city GDP, 2000-2018) with population, built-up area and road-network data; estimate scaling exponents, test curve collapse by comparing cross-city residual dispersion before and after rescaling, and compare out-of-sample predictions against a conditional-convergence regression.
ideas.disconfirming: Rescaled growth curves do not collapse (residual dispersion is unchanged), or the scaling model predicts worse out of sample than the convergence benchmark.

ideas.hypothesis: The negative association between natural-resource dependence and long-run growth is weaker in countries with generous R&D grants or tax credits, because fiscal innovation incentives pull capital and talent from rent-seeking resource sectors into innovative activity.

sources.role: mechanism: R&D grants and tax incentives raise market R&D, innovation and growth
finding: literature on the natural resources-growth relationship
mechanism: R&D as a driver of growth in endogenous growth models

ideas.test: Cross-country panel (about 80 countries, 1995-2018) with resource rents as a share of GDP (World Bank), R&D tax-subsidy rates (OECD B-index or similar) and per capita growth; growth regressions on 5-year averages with a resource rents x subsidy interaction, estimated with system GMM.
ideas.disconfirming: The interaction is zero or negative (subsidies deepen the curse), or it disappears once institutional quality is controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Shifting public spending from new construction toward maintenance raises the growth return of public capital, so regions with higher maintenance-to-investment ratios show a higher output elasticity of the public capital stock.

sources.role: mechanism: trade-offs between deferring maintenance and new projects under facility deterioration
finding: the composition of public expenditure changes its growth effect
setting: infrastructure as a driver of growth and competitiveness

ideas.test: Panel of US states (FHWA Highway Statistics, 1990-2018) or Chinese provinces with separate maintenance and capital outlays, pavement condition indices and gross state product; estimate production functions with public capital interacted with the maintenance share.
ideas.disconfirming: The maintenance share has no or a negative effect on the public capital elasticity, or growth rises with the new-construction share whatever the maintenance level.

ideas.hypothesis: High-frequency counts of taxi and ride-hailing trips carry information about current-quarter urban and national output growth beyond standard indicators, improving real-time growth nowcasts.

sources.role: measure: millions of taxi trip records as a fine-grained record of urban activity
method: in-sample and out-of-sample predictive tests of growth-related variables
mechanism: travel demand tied to land-use activity

ideas.test: NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission trip records (2009-2019) aggregated monthly, matched to metro and US GDP and employment; MIDAS nowcasting models with and without trip counts, compared by out-of-sample RMSE.
ideas.disconfirming: Trip counts do not reduce nowcast RMSE, or the gains vanish once payroll employment and retail sales are included.

ideas.hypothesis: The direction of export-growth causality depends on institutional quality: in transition economies with strong institutions exports Granger-cause growth, while in weak-institution economies causality runs only from growth to exports.

sources.role: finding: unidirectional causality from growth to exports in 13 transition economies
mechanism: institutional system quality conditions growth
mechanism: institutions as an endogenous growth variable

ideas.test: Panel of about 27 post-socialist economies, 1995-2018, with exports, GDP and Worldwide Governance Indicators or EBRD transition indices; split at the median institutional score and run Dumitrescu-Hurlin panel Granger causality tests in each group.
ideas.disconfirming: Causality patterns are the same in high- and low-institution groups, or exports fail to cause growth even where institutions are strong.

ideas.hypothesis: Generous pay-as-you-go social security reduces the growth payoff of a falling dependency ratio, because it crowds out the saving response that turns the demographic dividend into capital accumulation.

sources.role: mechanism: PAYG social security alters fertility, saving and growth depending on bequest motives
setting: population growth and economic growth in Pakistan

ideas.test: Cross-country panel (60-100 countries, 1970-2015) with working-age population share, pension replacement rates or pension spending (ILO/OECD), gross saving and per capita growth; growth regressions with a dependency change x pension generosity interaction and saving as a mediator.
ideas.disconfirming: The growth effect of the dividend is equal or larger in high-pension countries, or saving does not mediate the interaction.

ideas.hypothesis: Financial-sector liberalization raises growth only where overall economic freedom (property rights, regulation, trade openness) is above a threshold; below it liberalization has no or a negative growth effect.

sources.role: finding/method: positive growth effect of a financial reform dummy in Uganda
measure: economic freedom as a cross-country growth determinant

ideas.test: Panel of about 100 countries, 1975-2015, combining financial reform dates (Abiad et al. database), the Fraser economic freedom index and per capita growth; threshold regression of growth on liberalization with economic freedom as the threshold variable.
ideas.disconfirming: No threshold is found, or liberalization effects are the same at all freedom levels.

ideas.hypothesis: R&D tax incentives expand applied and experimental R&D but shift the mix away from basic research, so their growth effect is smaller where the basic-research share falls after introduction.

sources.role: finding: tax incentives complement market R&D and have the largest growth impact
mechanism: long waves rooted in clusters of fundamental technologies
mechanism: R&D in endogenous growth models

ideas.test: OECD MSTI data on R&D by type (basic, applied, experimental) for about 30 countries, 1990-2018, plus tax-subsidy indices; event study of incentive introductions on the basic share, then growth regressions with incentive x basic-share-change interaction.
ideas.disconfirming: The basic share does not fall after incentives are introduced, or the growth effect of incentives is unrelated to changes in R&D composition.

ideas.hypothesis: Fourth-quarter growth of a state or province predicts next-year returns of small-cap stocks headquartered there but not of large-cap stocks, because small firms' cash flows and investor bases are local.

sources.role: finding/method: fourth-quarter macro growth predicts returns of small- and large-cap portfolios
setting: local growth and its spillovers within a region

ideas.test: BEA quarterly state GDP (2005-2019) matched to CRSP/Compustat returns by headquarters state; predictive panel regressions of next-year returns on Q4 state growth, separately by size tercile, controlling for national Q4 growth.
ideas.disconfirming: State Q4 growth has no predictive power for local small caps, or it predicts equally well for large caps (pointing to a national factor).

ideas.hypothesis: A stochastic optimization model that allocates public spending across social, economic and administrative categories under uncertain returns gives a growth-maximizing mix that differs from actual allocations, and provinces closer to that optimum grow faster.

sources.role: method: stochastic optimization with an efficient solution algorithm for budget trade-offs
finding: social, economic and maintaining expenditures have different growth effects

ideas.test: Chinese provincial expenditure by function and GDP, 1995-2018; estimate category-specific return distributions, solve the stochastic program for each province, compute distance to the optimum and regress subsequent growth on that distance.
ideas.disconfirming: Distance to the optimum does not predict later growth, or the optimal shares are not robust to estimation noise.

ideas.hypothesis: In city-level growth accounting, ICT capital deepening and internet penetration explain a substantial share of the Solow residual, so adding ICT capital lowers the residual's contribution rate.

sources.role: mechanism: IT and internet as drivers of the new economy
method: contribution ratios of growth factors for a city

ideas.test: Chinese prefecture-city panel (2000-2018) with capital, labor, telecom investment and broadband subscriptions; growth accounting with and without ICT capital, comparing residual shares.
ideas.disconfirming: The residual share barely changes after adding ICT capital, or the ICT coefficients are insignificant.

ideas.hypothesis: Internet diffusion speeds conditional convergence: the convergence coefficient on initial income is larger among developing countries with faster growth in internet penetration.

sources.role: mechanism: internet expands access to knowledge and capabilities
method: relative growth and convergence measurement
method: cross-country growth regression with macro determinants

ideas.test: Cross-country panel 1995-2018 (WDI internet users, Penn World Table GDP per capita); beta-convergence regressions with an initial income x internet growth interaction and standard conditioning variables.
ideas.disconfirming: The interaction is insignificant, or it implies slower convergence where internet diffusion is faster.

ideas.hypothesis: Transit-oriented development around new rail stations raises employment density and job growth in station catchments by more than the jobs relocated from surrounding areas.

sources.role: mechanism: concentrating new development near transit services
finding: spillovers of nodal growth onto labor and enterprises
method: assessment of research designs for urban form effects

ideas.test: Difference-in-differences on station openings in one or more metros using LEHD LODES block-level jobs (2002-2018), comparing TOD-zoned catchments with planned-but-delayed stations, plus a ring analysis to measure displacement.
ideas.disconfirming: Catchment job gains are fully offset by losses in adjacent rings, or there is no gain relative to delayed-station controls.

ideas.hypothesis: Financial liberalization raises growth mainly by financing imports of capital goods, so post-reform growth gains are concentrated where capital-goods imports rise.

sources.role: finding: liberalization associated with higher growth in Uganda
finding: growth shaped by import demand in transition economies

ideas.test: Panel of about 40 reforming economies, 1980-2015, with reform dates, COMTRADE capital-goods imports and GDP growth; mediation analysis or panel VAR with imports between liberalization and growth.
ideas.disconfirming: Capital-goods imports do not rise after liberalization, or the growth effect is unchanged once imports are controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Exports cause growth only once human capital passes a threshold that allows absorption of foreign technology; below it growth-led exports dominate.

sources.role: finding: growth-led rather than export-led growth in transition economies
mechanism: human capital and R&D in endogenous growth
setting: contribution of education to growth

ideas.test: Panel of about 100 countries, 1970-2015, with Barro-Lee schooling, exports and GDP; panel threshold model of export-to-growth causality with average schooling as the threshold variable.
ideas.disconfirming: No schooling threshold appears, or export-led causality is equally weak above and below it.

ideas.hypothesis: Using average adult height as the output series in an S-shaped relative growth model classifies regions much as GDP does in rich regions but diverges in poor ones, revealing growth episodes without matching welfare gains.

sources.role: method: S-shaped relative growth model classifying growth, development and underdevelopment
mechanism: divergence in living standards as the core growth question
setting: historical market revolution with uneven welfare across classes

ideas.test: Italian regional conscript height data and regional GDP (e.g., 1900-1980), or DHS adult heights by region in developing countries; apply the relative growth model to both series and compare classifications.
ideas.disconfirming: Height- and GDP-based classifications agree everywhere, or heights show no relation to measured growth.

ideas.hypothesis: Early regional differences in urbanization and market integration are amplified over time, so initial urban share predicts a widening North-South income gap with coefficients that grow rather than shrink across decades.

sources.role: setting: market revolution, urbanization and sectional divergence between North and South
mechanism: overflow (spread) and backwash effects between nodes and hinterlands
method: relative growth measurement across regions

ideas.test: US county census data 1820-1900 (urban share, manufacturing output, income proxies) or Italian provinces; rolling regressions of growth on initial urbanization, testing for rising coefficients and sigma-divergence.
ideas.disconfirming: Initial urban share predicts convergence, or its effect fades over time.

ideas.hypothesis: Population growth raises per capita growth only in economies with high economic freedom, where markets absorb a growing labor force; in low-freedom economies the association is negative.

sources.role: finding: positive population-growth relationship in Pakistan
measure: economic freedom index as a growth determinant

ideas.test: Cross-country panel, 1980-2015, of 5-year averages with the Fraser index, population growth and per capita GDP growth; interaction regressions with country fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: The interaction is zero or negative.

ideas.hypothesis: Metropolitan areas that adopt smart-growth policies (compact, mixed-use, transit-oriented development) see higher productivity growth through agglomeration and lower travel costs than comparable metros without them.

sources.role: setting: content of smart-growth strategies
method: critique of research designs linking urban form to outcomes
mechanism: density raises efficiency of shared trips

ideas.test: US metros 1990-2015: code adoption of state or regional smart-growth laws and use BEA metro GDP per worker; staggered difference-in-differences or synthetic control.
ideas.disconfirming: No productivity difference, or smart-growth metros grow more slowly because of housing constraints.

ideas.hypothesis: Improvements in electricity supply reliability raise new enterprise formation more in hinterland districts than in nodal centres.

sources.role: mechanism: infrastructure as a determinant of growth and competitiveness
setting/measure: enterprise development across nodal and hinterland areas in South Sulawesi

ideas.test: District panel for Indonesia using utility electrification and outage data and economic census firm counts (2006, 2016); difference-in-differences comparing districts with grid upgrades vs without, split by nodal/hinterland status.
ideas.disconfirming: Firm formation does not respond, or responds equally in nodal and hinterland districts.

ideas.hypothesis: Population growth raises per capita output growth only where road infrastructure keeps pace; when road stock per capita falls, population growth turns growth-reducing through congestion.

sources.role: finding: population growth and growth in Pakistan
mechanism: rising travel demand and highway deterioration
mechanism: infrastructure and competitiveness

ideas.test: District panel for Pakistan or state panel for India (1990-2015) with population, road kilometres and output; interaction regressions and dynamic panel estimates.
ideas.disconfirming: The effect of population growth does not depend on road density.

ideas.hypothesis: Where family transfers are altruistic rather than exchange-based, migrant remittances respond to recipient income shocks rather than to services received, and remittance inflows have larger growth effects through household human capital investment.

sources.role: mechanism: distinguishing altruistic, exchange, joy-of-giving and accidental transfer motives with testable implications
setting: Pakistan, with large emigration and population growth

ideas.test: Household panel (e.g., Pakistan PSLM or Mexico MxFLS) linking remittances to recipient income shocks and services to parents; classify dominant motives, then regress district growth and schooling on remittances by motive.
ideas.disconfirming: Remittance responses do not separate motives, or growth effects are the same whatever the motive.

ideas.hypothesis: Adding an index of institutional change (e.g., marketization) to provincial growth accounting absorbs a large part of the TFP residual, implying measured TFP partly reflects institutional reform.

sources.role: method: contribution ratios of growth factors
mechanism: institution as an endogenous growth variable
mechanism: system change and growth

ideas.test: Chinese provinces 1997-2016 with the Fan-Wang marketization index, capital, labor and output; compare residual contribution before and after including marketization in an augmented production function.
ideas.disconfirming: The residual is largely unchanged, or marketization adds no explanatory power.

ideas.hypothesis: Metropolitan areas where average commute times fall (through urban form or transit) see faster per capita income growth over the following decade because workers reach larger effective labor markets.

sources.role: mechanism: urban form shapes travel behavior
measure: trip-level urban mobility data
setting: growth-corridor housing development with car-dependent travel

ideas.test: US metro panel with Census/ACS commute times (1990-2017) and BEA per capita income; regress decadal income growth on change in commute times, instrumenting with planned highway or transit openings.
ideas.disconfirming: No relation, or income grows faster where commutes lengthen.

ideas.hypothesis: Regions with stronger social ties to economically dynamic regions grow faster, because social networks transmit information and investment spillovers from nodal centres.

sources.role: measure: social connectedness as an outcome of community design
mechanism: overflow effects of growth centres on surrounding regions

ideas.test: US counties: Facebook Social Connectedness Index with BEA county income growth 2010-2019; regress growth on SCI-weighted growth of connected counties, controlling for distance-weighted neighbor growth.
ideas.disconfirming: SCI-weighted growth has no effect once distance-weighted growth is controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Tax revenue growth departs from output growth systematically with the output gap: the tax-output elasticity exceeds one above potential and falls below one below it, so tax-growth gaps carry information on potential growth.

sources.role: finding: tax growth fluctuates around economic growth and they equilibrate in the long run
setting: fiscal aggregates and growth in China

ideas.test: Quarterly tax revenue and GDP for about 30 countries, 1990-2019, with OECD/IMF potential output; asymmetric error-correction models with output-gap interactions, and tests of whether tax gaps predict later revisions to potential output.
ideas.disconfirming: The elasticity is constant across output-gap states and tax gaps do not predict revisions to potential.

ideas.hypothesis: Creating a special economic zone raises the host region's intra-industry trade share, marking a shift from a 'barring' to an 'introducing' growth pattern through integration into international production networks.

sources.role: mechanism: introducing pattern via integration into the international division of labor and intra-industry trade
measure: trade-growth relations

ideas.test: Chinese prefecture or provincial customs data 1995-2010 with SEZ establishment dates; compute Grubel-Lloyd indices and run staggered difference-in-differences.
ideas.disconfirming: Grubel-Lloyd indices do not rise after SEZs are established.

ideas.hypothesis: In transition economies, consumer confidence shocks drive import demand, which in turn leads output growth, accounting for the import-shaped growth pattern.

sources.role: finding: growth shaped by rising import demand in transition economies
mechanism: economic growth correlates with growth in consumer confidence

ideas.test: Quarterly EU Commission consumer confidence, imports and GDP for 10 new EU members, 1995-2019; structural VAR with confidence ordered first and imports between confidence and output.
ideas.disconfirming: Confidence shocks do not move imports, or imports do not lead output.

ideas.hypothesis: Deeper participation in the international division of labor (global value chains) accelerates domestic knowledge accumulation in developing countries, measured by patents citing foreign prior art.

sources.role: mechanism: using frontier technology by joining the international division of labor
mechanism: knowledge and R&D in endogenous growth
mechanism: diffusion of technology clusters

ideas.test: Panel of about 50 developing countries, 1995-2015, with OECD TiVA participation indices and PATSTAT patents and citations; dynamic panel with lagged GVC participation.
ideas.disconfirming: GVC participation does not predict knowledge accumulation.

ideas.hypothesis: Trade liberalization raised youth unemployment in more tariff-exposed Indian districts in the short run but lowered it within a decade as export sectors expanded.

sources.role: setting: before-after analysis of Indian trade liberalization
finding: trade-growth causality patterns

ideas.test: District-level tariff exposure from pre-reform industry mix and NSS employment rounds 1987-2011; difference-in-differences comparing youth with adults across horizons.
ideas.disconfirming: Youth unemployment shows no differential response to tariff exposure at any horizon.
